strategy.summary:
Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd is a sound, family-owned bearing distributor for whom we are a small account. Its sales side is refocusing on key accounts and has called us 'not strategic'. It still asked to renew the framework covering all three bearings and wants our volumes. Its stated doctrine is that standard items carry list prices and only multi-year volume agreements change prices.

Cost drivers justify well under one percent. Its renewal asks have historically settled far below the ask.

Our position differs by part:
- 360020: dual-sourced. The rival is cheaper on current orders, but its fresh RFQ quote is higher.
- 360021: near price parity with the rival, which already holds the majority quota.
- 360022: single source for the HI series, so supply security dominates.

Performance has slipped. On-time delivery is well below the contractual target, worst on 360020, and ppm has risen but remains better than the peer median.

The winning formula is a bundled multi-year volume agreement, offered through the cooperative owner channel, in exchange for a hold or a minimal increase.
strategy.decision_maker: The owner of the family firm (he offered open-book costing). The new sales director runs the 'not strategic' account review, so route the substantive price discussion to the owner where possible.

persona.owner_type: family-owned GmbH, distributor/stockist of standard bearings, 120 staff
persona.style: Doctrine-driven sales side (list prices, key-account focus), slower replies since summer. Owner is pragmatic and open to fact-based costing talk.

Says only multi-year volume agreements move prices
Contradictory signals: says it won't extend individual agreements, yet asks to renew and wants our volumes

needs.detail: Wants accounts with volume. It asked for our expected volumes and says only multi-year volume deals change prices.
Values multi-year binding agreements over yearly individual renegotiation.
Wants to streamline small accounts toward standard stock and list conditions, i.e. less handling effort per account. A bundled single agreement covering all three parts fits this.
The owner seeks a fair, fact-based settlement and offered to show hourly rates and material.

constraints.detail: We are labelled 'not strategic' and replies are slower. It may let the individual agreement lapse and serve us from list.
360022 has no other approved source. We have never run an RFQ for it, and it serves the HI pump series.
Prices are fixed per calendar year. Changes need written notice before year end. The framework auto-renews unless terminated with notice. The termination window is still open on both sides.
No should-cost exists for any part, so the margin cannot be measured. The evidence on its true cost is thin.

levers.why: Clear volume growth on 360021 speaks directly to its 'customers with volume' focus. It also answers its request for expected volumes.
Shows stable-to-growing demand on its largest part with us, as a basis for a binding multi-year bundle.
The bearing PPI justifies only a fraction of any ask. It fits the owner's open-book offer.
Labour adds only marginally, given its small cost share.
Accept the owner's open-calculation offer. This moves the talk to facts and to the decision maker.
On-time delivery is well below the contractual target and falling. It argues against paying more for a worsening service. Use it factually, not as a threat.
It habitually settles well below its ask, so its opening is not the anchor.
The rival is at parity and holds the majority quota on 360021. Quota growth there is ours to give.
Steady demand on the single-source part supports a bundled multi-year agreement.
We are a reliable payer with no discount abuse. Supporting goodwill.
Recurring defects on 360020 serve as a fresh-fact filler in a later round.
Caps the justified increase on the single-source part.

trades.why: It explicitly says only multi-year agreements move prices. Twenty-four months captures the value.
Binding volume, including a larger quota share on 360021/360020 within our need, is its main currency.
Thirty days is already short of our standard, and the supplier has no cash need. Don't spend money buying a faster payment, but don't ask for long payment either.
Stock supply at its standard lead time suits it. Asking for shorter would be priced.
Quality has slipped. A ppm target secures quality at little cost to it if it wants to keep the account.

price_view.reasoning: Drivers justify under one percent, and past renewals settled at a fraction of the ask. However, it is sound, sees us as small and is shifting to list pricing. On 360020 the rival's fresh quote is higher than this supplier's, which weakens any switching threat. On 360021 a hold is realistic. On 360022 we have no benchmark and must protect supply. A realistic outcome is a hold or a minimal increase, bought with a multi-year bundled volume commitment.

strategy.writer_notes: Lead with volume and a bundled multi-year agreement covering all three bearings. Reply to its renewal mail with our forecast. Propose taking up the owner's calculation walk-through, and set the bearing index facts against any ask. Hold the delivery shortfall and quality record back as fresh facts for later rounds, phrased as joint improvement. Keep the second source in the background, and never present it as a threat. Protect the single-source part first. Make shrinking real steps paired with a new argument each round. Accept a declared final offer if it beats the fallback.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for any of the three bearings, so how far prices sit above full cost cannot be measured directly. The only proxies are the index drivers, rival prices and price history. The owner offered to walk us through their calculation, which would be the way to close this gap.

The cost drivers justify almost nothing. PPI-C2815 is +0.8% over 12 months (weights 0.63-0.66), giving about +0.5% on the price. LCI-C is +2.7% (weights 0.09-0.12), giving about +0.24-0.32%. The combined justified increase is roughly +0.8% per part. Both indices sit at their 36-month peak, so they give no case for a reduction either. Since 2023 our prices rose +4.8% to +6.6% while PPI-C2815 rose only +3.7% from its low, so cumulative pricing has outrun the bearing index.

Part 360020 (6306): the supplier now quotes 4.63 for 90 days in the second-source RFQ, +5.5% on the current 4.39. That ask is far above the roughly +0.8% the drivers justify. Its own list quote of 4.39, valid 7 days and from stock, holds the current price. The rival sup:70640 supplies at 4.20 (-4.3%) on its 30% quota. However, the rival's fresh RFQ quote is 5.04, which undercuts any 'cheaper elsewhere' threat. Its renewal history shows an average ask of +5.1% settled at +2.1%.

Part 360021 (6308): price unchanged at 7.23 since 2025. The rival sup:70640 is at 7.21 and won the 2024 RFQ at 7.15 against this supplier's 7.42. There is effective price parity, and this supplier holds only a 40% quota. A small reduction or a hold is defensible.
Part 360022 (7309 BEP): single source. The latest quote of 22.8 holds the price, at list conditions and from stock only. There is no external benchmark, so this is the weakest price position.

Market news on copper, electronic boards and steel does not apply to these bearing drivers. The relevant driver index, PPI-C2815, shows only +0.8%. We are a small customer, at 0.5% of its turnover, and the supplier is shifting to list pricing. Price room is therefore thin: the realistic aim is to hold current prices or concede about +1%, with more volume offered as the trade.

findings.text: Strategic shift away from small accounts: Their management (sales director, now a new sales director) is deliberately refocusing on key accounts and new product lines. Hollerau has been explicitly labelled 'not strategic'. Replies have slowed since summer. The sales side is not motivated by our account as it stands.

Stated pricing doctrine: standard items are not discounted and are supplied from stock at list conditions. Individual agreements will 'not be extended'. Only multi-year volume agreements change prices. This makes a longer contract term plus binding or higher volume the main currency for any concession.

Contradiction between the July and September letters. In July they said individual agreements would not be extended, yet on 2026-09-20 they asked to renew ctr:4600070620 and requested our expected volumes. They still want the business if the volume is attractive. Our forecast volumes rise on all three parts (part:360021 by about 16%).

The owner is an alternative and more cooperative channel. In June he offered an open-book walk-through of hourly rates and material. In this family firm, decisions plausibly sit with the owner rather than the new sales director. Open costing invites a fact-based discussion, and the cost drivers are weak: PPI bearings +0.8% and labour +2.7% on a small cost share.

Financially sound and stable. Family-owned, founded 1975, 120 staff, EUR 46.8M turnover, 34% equity ratio, credit index 181 unchanged, VDA 6.3 grade A. Our spend is only about 0.5% of their turnover. There is no cash stress for us to exploit, and they can afford to lose us.

Payment behaviour is fair but slightly late: 2.9 days after due on average, 84.9% of invoices late, maximum 11 days, no discount abuse. This gives modest goodwill. Paying strictly on time, or faster, is a cheap gesture they may value.
Earlier relationship warmth: a trade fair invitation in December 2025. Their tone has since cooled. The evidence on personalities is thin; there are only short notes.

findings.text: Framework ctr:4600070620 covers all three bearings, runs to 2026-12-31 and renews automatically for 12 months unless either side gives 60 days' notice, i.e. by 2026-11-01. Prices are fixed per calendar year. A change for 2027 needed written notice 60 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-11-01. The supplier's 2026-09-20 mail treats the agreement as expiring, and its 2026-07-06 mail says individual agreements will not be extended. Expect it to terminate and move us to list conditions rather than let the agreement auto-renew.

Other obligations: payment 30 days net, which is shorter than our 60-day standard and so a concession already given; DAP; 7-day lead time; 95% on-time target; flat EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint. Delivery is at 85% on time, well below the 95% target and down from 88.9% a year ago. That breach is our strongest contractual lever.

Renewal history: the supplier asks for 1.6-7.1% and settles at roughly 40% of the ask. Average asks and settlements were 5.1%→2.1% (360020), 3.7%→1.6% (360021) and 3.6%→1.6% (360022). Four of the nine renewals settled at 0%. The last round gave 2.3% on 360020 and 0% on the others. Prices are up 4.8-6.6% since 2023 and have never fallen.

Dependency is mixed by part. 360020: we have a dual source, the supplier holds a 70% quota, and sup:70640 currently delivers at EUR 4.20 against our 4.39. 360021: the supplier holds only 40% and the rival is at 7.21 against 7.23, so it is easily replaceable. 360022: the supplier is our 100% single source with no RFQ ever run. The library claims supplier-owned tooling, but the sourcing data says tooling n/a for these catalogue bearings, so the evidence conflicts. Treat the tooling lock-in as weak.

The supplier depends little on us. We are about 0.5% of its turnover, at EUR 217k in FY2026. It is financially sound, and it has repeatedly said small accounts are no longer strategic: standard items at list prices, discounts only for multi-year volume deals. Threats to leave carry little weight with it.

findings.text: Delivery has deteriorated steadily: rolling OTD (requested date) fell from 94.5% (2024Q3) to 85.0% (2026Q3), against the contract target of 95%. A year earlier it was 88.9%. Against its own confirmed dates it reaches only 86.2%. Late deliveries average 12-14 days, with a maximum of 33 days. The scorecard still shows class A/green, which flatters it. Peers' median is 84.6%, so it is only average among peers.

Late delivery is concentrated on part:360020 (6306-2Z). Over the last 12 months it delivered 75.9% on time, 24.1% of receipts were late, and the worst was 33 days late. part:360021 delivered 88.5% on time. part:360022, our single source, delivered 92% on time.

Quality has worsened. Rolling ppm rose from 36-37 (2024) to a peak of 387 (2025Q4) and stands at 302 now. Complaints rose from 1 to 9-11 a year. That is still below the peers' median of 457 ppm, and no 8D report is overdue, so the supplier can present quality as acceptable. On part:360020 the rival sup:70640 had 0 ppm over the last 12 months while this supplier had 299 ppm. Recurring defect types are porosity, missing marking, wrong material certificates and burrs, which points to a systemic process problem.

The cost of poor quality to us is only partly recovered. 15 supplier-caused QNs have been raised since 2024; the €150 flat fee was recharged on only about 10 of them, and 5 recent ones show €0 recharged. These include qn:20004857 and qn:20004869, plus qn:20004461, qn:20004477 and qn:20004732.

Our volume outlook is stable to growing, and the forecasts are shared with the supplier. part:360020: 28,600 forecast for the next 12 months against 27,440 ordered over the last 12 months (all suppliers). part:360021: 17,330 against 14,940. part:360022: 3,880 against 3,780. This is still small for the supplier: our spend is about €217k, roughly 0.5% of its turnover, and it says it now focuses on key accounts.

Its prices sit above the second source on the shared parts. On part:360020 it charges €4.39 against €4.20 from sup:70640, which also has better quality. On part:360021 it charges €7.23 against €7.21. Its prices have risen 4.8-6.6% since 2023.

Order handling: we placed rush and changed lines with it (360021: 4 rush, 7 changed). It has 12 partial and 9 over-delivered lines. Requested and confirmed dates differ partly because of a known data issue, so delivery figures should be cited from the scorecard.

arguments.text: The benchmark is on my side for 360020. Your own second-source RFQ brought a quote from Inntal at 5.04 EUR. My current 4.39 EUR is well below that. Even my 8,580-pc quote at 4.63 EUR beats it. Switching volume away from us would cost you more, not less.

360022 (7309 BEP for the HI series) has no other approved source. We have supplied it 100 % since 2014. The price was held at 22.80 EUR for 2026 despite rising forecasts. Stable supply from stock has a value, and list conditions are fair.

Our costs are rising. Labour costs in manufacturing are up 2.7 % year on year, and steel is up 7.3 % since January. We held 360021 and 360022 flat for 2026 and took only 2.3 % on 360020. Over three years, that is far below our asks.

Individual prices are an exception now. Our policy is that standard items come from stock at list conditions, and only multi-year volume agreements change prices. That applies to every account of your size, not just to you.
We are a sound, stable partner: family-owned since 1975, 34 % equity ratio, VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001/14001. Every 8D has been closed with nothing overdue, and our scorecard is still class A / green.

weak_points: On-time delivery is 85 % over the last 12 months against the contractual 95 %. On 360020 it is only 75.9 %, with up to 33 days late. Our sales notes concede this is the worst part.
Ppm rose from about 36 to about 300. There were 9 complaints in the last 12 months, against zero ppm for Inntal on 360020 and 360021.
The PPI for bearings rose only +0.8 % in 12 months and carries a weight of about 0.63. Cost drivers justify well under 1 %.
Our own quote at 4.63 EUR for 8,580 pcs undercuts our list story and shows room. The 4.39 EUR list quote has only 7 days' validity.
Inntal holds 60 % of 360021 at 7.21 EUR, practically at our 7.23 EUR. We are easy to replace there.
History shows our renewal asks settled at a fraction of the ask, often at zero.
Our owner offered to open the calculation (hourly rates, material). If purchasing takes him up on it, the margin shows.
They pay on average 3 days late, but that is a minor point for us. Calling them 'not strategic' may look like a bluff if we then want their volume.
wants: A bundled multi-year agreement (24-36 months) covering all three bearings, with committed annual volumes of about 28,600 / 17,300 / 3,900 pcs.
A higher quota on 360020, ideally 100 %, and more on 360021.
Faster payment, e.g. 14 days, or at least on time.
Smoothed call-offs from stock with fewer rush and change lines.
In return I would hold 2026 prices on 360021 and 360022 and limit 360020 to about 0-1.5 %.
red_lines: No price cuts below current 2026 prices without a multi-year volume commitment.
No individual one-year agreement at special terms; for a single year, list conditions apply.
No raised chargeback above 150 EUR per complaint or a binding ppm penalty without a price offset.
No acceptance of a fixed price beyond 12 months without a volume commitment or a steel/labour index clause.
red_team.opening: Thank you for 12 years of cooperation. Under our range reorganisation, we would supply from stock at list prices: 360020 at 4.63 EUR (+5.5 %), 360021 at 7.45 EUR (+3 %), and 360022 at 23.60 EUR (+3.5 %), citing labour costs and steel. I would immediately point out that a bundled 3-year volume agreement on all three parts with a higher quota on 360020 is the one way to stay close to current prices. I would also ask for the expected volumes.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that the fresh second-source quote is above your current price, and we value that your offer is competitive. That is exactly why we want to keep and grow the volume with you rather than move it. At the same time, the price we pay today is the reference for any renewal, and the second source supplies the same bearing at a lower price on current orders, so the benchmark is not one-sided. Our proposal is a multi-year volume agreement at today's price, not a switch.

We fully acknowledge your long, sole supply of this bearing for our HI series and the price you held this year. Supply security matters most to us here, which is why we want to include it in a multi-year agreement with steady volumes rather than leave it on short-validity list quotes. The bearing cost index justifies only a small fraction of a percent, so we see the current price as the fair basis going forward.

We appreciate the restraint of recent renewals. Labour costs did rise, but labour is a small share of a stocked bearing, so its effect on the price is marginal. Basic steel prices are not the right measure for finished bearings; the producer price index for bearings, which is the relevant driver, has barely moved over the year. Together these support well under one percent, which a multi-year volume commitment more than compensates.

We understand and respect the policy, and we propose exactly what it allows: one bundled multi-year agreement covering all three bearings with binding volumes, which also reduces your handling effort per account. You asked for our expected volumes; our forecasts show stable or growing demand on all three parts, notably on the deep groove bearings.

The scorecard colour, however, hides a clear trend: on-time delivery is well below the contractual target and has fallen over the year, and complaints have risen. We would like to fix this together, with a ppm and delivery commitment in the new agreement, rather than pay more for a weakening service.
